newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Treasury to submit budget cuts on Dec 9.
newsitem.headline: Israel Treasury to submit budget cuts on Dec 9.

text.p: The Treasury plans to submit to the government on December 9 a proposal for a second round of cuts to the 1997 budget, Treasury sources said on Tuesday.
Finance Minister Dan Meridor has not announced a specific date but on Tuesday he said the Treasury expects to finalise the size and composition of spending cuts needed in 1997 next week.
"We had talks yesterday, also this morning. During this week and next week we will conclude the talks concerning both the size of the cut needed and the composition," he told Israel Radio.
Last week, he and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced plans for an additional cut of about two billion shekels from next year's 190.8 billion shekel budget.
After they receive cabinet approval the additional budget cuts will be sent to parliament, which has until the end of December to pass the spending package.
Legislators, meanwhile, are still haggling over the government's original budget proposal, which included a hefty 4.9 billion shekel cut.
Meridor declined to comment on the Bank of Israel's decision to leave interest rates unchanged in December despite a drop in the bond market's inflationary expectations for the next 12 months.
The central bank's decision is seen by many in the business sector as an attempt to put pressure on the government to implement stiff budget cuts.
The central bank maintains it cannot ease monetary policy until the government curbs spending.
